title: Case: Customs duty amount disputed between broker and depot scan
context: A parcel is held at customs pending duty payment. The appointed broker and the depot have submitted conflicting figures for the assessed duty. The desk must route the conflict to the party that can reconcile it.
initial_request: Resolve which duty amount is correct so payment can proceed.

events.body: DL-978 held pending duty. Invoice value £340, tariff code 6204.62.20, origin China. Calculated duty: £68.00 at 20% rate plus £2.50 admin fee. Total £70.50 payable by shipper.

events.from: Plover Arc Logistics Gatwick depot, parcel trace
events.body: DL-978 scanned on arrival. Customs declaration shows duty assessed at £65.20. Awaiting shipper payment instruction before release.

events.from: Malik Sethi, Brineleaf Pantry refunds team
events.body: Shipper (us) received two different duty figures from your broker and depot. £70.50 vs £65.20. Which do we pay? Customer is demanding the parcel. We need clarity before approving payment to avoid overpayment or clearance delay.

acceptable_actions.summary: Request confirmation of the duty amount and reconciliation with the depot's scanned assessment of £65.20.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Plover Arc Logistics Gatwick depot, parcel trace
acceptable_actions.summary: Request confirmation of the scanned duty figure and reconciliation with the broker's calculation of £70.50.

must: Send the conflicting figures (£70.50 and £65.20) to the party responsible for resolving them
Do not instruct the shipper to pay either amount
Do not assume which figure is correct based on source alone
must_not: Tell the shipper to pay the broker's figure without verification
Tell the shipper to pay the depot's figure without verification
Instruct either team to adjust their assessment without investigation
Escalate to a supervisor when the desk can route to the responsible resolver
expected.reference_message: Keswick Customs House: the depot scan shows duty assessed at £65.20 on arrival, but your broker portal message states £70.50. Please confirm which figure is correct and advise how to reconcile the difference so the shipper can pay and the parcel can be cleared.

rationale: The broker and depot disagree on the duty amount; neither source has proven authority over the other at this stage. The desk must not pick a side or guess. The appointed broker is responsible for duty calculation and customs clearance decisions, so they are the correct party to resolve the discrepancy with the depot's scan record and confirm the accurate payable amount.
